jobs.prompt:
Create ONE production game sprite, an entirely new mounted Sun Li for a historical Chinese Song-dynasty isometric RTS. The FIRST reference supplies Sun Li's facial identity, dark iron helmet silhouette, dark gold-trimmed lamellar armor, brown under-robe, sturdy build, and back-carried bow/quiver. The SECOND reference supplies ONLY the horse-and-rider scale and high 3/4 isometric camera angle; do NOT copy that soldier's face, spear or costume.
Output actual RGBA PNG with TRANSPARENT empty background, alpha zero; no backdrop, checkerboard, ground plane, cast shadow, text or border. One complete horse and one rider, centered with generous transparent margins. Full hooves, ears, tail, rider's helmet and weapon tip inside the canvas. Hand-painted realistic classic RTS game art, restrained dark brown/black/gold palette, clear small-scale silhouette, soft upper-left lighting.
Sun Li now rides a solid BLACK warhorse (black mane and tail, natural dark highlights, no white socks or face blaze). Plain dark brown Chinese saddle, muted brown saddle cloth, leather bridle and stirrups. Horse faces SOUTHEAST toward screen LOWER RIGHT, its front and rightward-facing side visible, consistent 30-degree downward viewing camera. Horse calm, all four correct anatomical legs distinct in a grounded standing pose. Rider seated naturally astride saddle, exactly two arms/two legs, boots resting in stirrups.
Identity: mature Chinese officer, stern square face, short black beard and moustache, dark iron helmet with the same small crossed upward projections as the first reference, black/oiled iron armor edged in muted gold, brown robe skirt and belt, bow and quiver secured diagonally on his back. No Japanese samurai styling, no cape hiding the horse anatomy.
Weapon correction: his anatomical RIGHT hand grips ONE rigid bamboo-node iron mace (Chinese gangbian): a solid straight black steel rod about the length of his forearm plus upper arm, eight raised ring-shaped nodes along the shaft, small gold handle, rounded BLUNT tip. It is NOT a flexible whip, rope, chain, curved bow, sword, axe or spear. Right hand holds the mace diagonally downward toward the lower right in a relaxed guard, fully visible outside the horse body. His anatomical LEFT hand holds the reins at saddle height. Keep these two separate hand functions obvious. No extra hand, duplicate weapon, dangling chain or polearm. The only bow is strapped on the BACK.

LAYOUT: 2 columns by 4 rows, EIGHT full mounted-unit poses, read left to right then top to bottom. Large equal cells and generous clear blank gaps. Pose 1: IDLE. Rider upright in saddle, mace low in right-hand guard, left hand reins. Horse standing with four grounded legs.
Pose 2: WALK A, a slow horse trot, front LEFT and rear RIGHT legs reaching forward, the opposite diagonal pair trailing. Rider sitting low and steady, hands retain their roles, mace held low.
Pose 3: WALK B, opposite diagonal of the horse's trot: front RIGHT and rear LEFT legs reaching forward, opposite diagonal pair trailing. Genuinely change the horse legs, not just duplicate pose 2 or shift the entire bitmap. Rider steady, mace low.
Pose 4: ATTACK WINDUP. Horse plants its feet; rider turns shoulders slightly, raises his RIGHT hand and rigid mace high behind his right shoulder for a forceful diagonal downward club strike. Left hand holds reins at saddle. Exactly two arms.
Pose 5: ATTACK IMPACT. Same planted horse and scale. Rider leans forward and drives the RIGHT-hand rigid mace down/forward at an enemy just ahead on the facing diagonal. Mace is now extended near horse head height, different from both idle and windup. Left hand still reins. No enemy or effects drawn.
Pose 6: HURT. Rider recoils in the saddle, torso twists backward, right hand still grips mace, left reins. Horse dips neck and braces, remains standing and alive.
Pose 7: FALL. Horse is collapsing to its side with knees folded, rider falling off that same side beside the saddle; a coherent single mounted unit in mid-collapse. Keep both full bodies intact and visible, same anatomy and size. No gore, no extra horse or rider.
Pose 8: DOWN. Horse lies fully on its side with four legs naturally folded/extended on the ground, rider lies motionless beside the saddle, his rigid mace on the ground near his right hand. Both bodies same scale as earlier poses, no floating rider, no missing horse, no gore.
All eight poses must keep the requested facing. All four horse legs and two human arms/legs must attach plausibly; reins only in left hand, short rigid mace only in right. Do not mirror to fake facing.
